title: Crew Habitat Brief and Cadence Reset
summary: Quarterly operational reset focused on cadence, hiring priorities, and incident postures. Leadership presented metrics on burn, runway, hiring, Dedicated & Private launch timelines, and a new cadence for cross-functional 'squad huddles'. Open Q&A covered oncall rotations, compensation calibration, and a pilot for a reliability bounty program.
topics: Company health: burn runway and hiring speed
Product milestones: Dedicated GA plans and Private pilot timeline
Operational cadence: squad huddles, incident runbooks, oncall rotation
Hiring and org structure: IC ladders and manager spans
Reliability & SLOs: incident review cadence and bounty pilot
People ops: compensation timing and parental leave update
action_items: Priya: Publish Dedicated GA checklist and rollout timeline; due 2027-09-28
Diego: Share proposed oncall rota and escalation playbook draft; due 2027-09-21
Oliver: Circulate updated hiring budget and headcount delta; due 2027-09-20
Avery: Run compensation calibration forum and record notes; due 2027-09-24
Nora: Prototype reliability bounty workflow and sample task list; due 2027-10-05
next_steps: Leadership to approve revised hiring priorities by end of week
Product to schedule Dedicated GA dry-run with SEs and SREs next Wednesday
People to open forum for IC ladder feedback and collect comments
transcription:
Meeting header: 2027-09-14 10:00 PDT / Duration ~78m / Attendees listed above

[00:00] Avery Chen: All right team, let's get started, um, thanks for making time. We have a pretty packed deck — but we'll keep it tight. Quick ask, please mute unless you're speaking.

[00:18] Maya Rivera (CEO): Good morning, everyone. Quick opener: big thanks for hitting the Dedicated beta numbers last month, that was — that was really strong. Today is less about a product demo and more about resetting how we ship and how we run on a weekly basis.

[00:35] Liam O'Connor (CTO): Quick data point — platform errors are down 12% month-over-month but latency tail rose slightly during spikes on the west region. We have capacity hotspots, especially when large batch imports hit the VPC gateways. We'll talk mitigation later.

[00:52] Priya Kapoor (VP Product): I'll cover the Dedicated GA timeline and the Private pilot. Key dates: internal dry-run 9/22, partner pilot 10/11, target GA 11/15. These are aggressive but achievable if org prioritizes a few things — testing, docs, and SRE readiness.

[01:12] Maya: Important callout — customers are asking for stronger audit logs and KMS integrations for Private. That is a sales blocker for some mid-market accounts.

[01:30] Renee Park (Head of Revenue): Yep, on demos I've been hearing SSO and KMS first, encryption at rest. Also we need a clearer pricing example for Dedicated to use in RFPs. Customers want predictable throughput numbers for X tokens per second in a reserved pool.

[01:50] Diego Morales (Head of Engineering): On that, the Dedicated perf profile doc is being updated. We'll add a short spreadsheet that maps GPU types to throughput per-model; also add recommended batch sizes and latency SLOs.

[02:06] Oliver Zhang (CFO): Finance perspective: current burn is within plan but runway shortens if we don't moderate hiring in Q4. We're proposing shifting a few non-critical roles to H1 next year. We'll need leadership alignment.

[02:25] Maya: Let's be explicit, we can't stall key infra roles — SRE and core serving runtime. Some product hiring can wait.

[02:40] Nora Singh (Staff ML Eng): On reliability — suggested we enable read-only kvcache metrics in staging and allow SEs to run synthetic prefix-caching tests. The current KV cache visibility is a bit opaque for new models and sequence lengths.

[03:01] Priya: Good. We'll roll that into the dry-run plan.

[03:08] -- Topic shift: Cadence --

[03:10] Avery: We want to try a new "squad huddle" cadence: 15-min cross-functional sync twice a week per squad, plus a weekly ops triage. Purpose: reduce email, speed escalation, and get alignment on immediate blockers. Thoughts?

[03:29] Diego: I'd prefer twice weekly but flexible timing. Also proposal: rotate one engineering PM into the huddle as a lead so follow-ups don't slip.

[03:41] Priya: We'll pilot with Infra Squad and Eval Squad for three weeks. If it reduces async threads by 30% we'll expand.

[03:50] -- Q&A starts --

[03:51] Employee (unlabeled): Question on oncall— will we expand the pool or increase ops support?

[03:58] Diego: Short answer: expand pool with guardrails. We'll rework the pager rules so infra pages go to SRE first and only escalate to engineers if needed. Also planning to add a weekend backup for Dedicated live customers.

[04:14] Liam: Also adding a thinner alert tier — info-level that lands in a channel not a pager to reduce noise.

[04:27] -- Finance / Hiring --

[04:29] Oliver: Headcount ask — prior plan was +22 hires. We're recommending taking that to +14 now and re-evaluating in Q1. The ask from product and sales is understandable but runway is tight.

[04:42] Renee: Sales impact — if we slow hiring for customer-facing SEs we might hamper Dedicated uptake. Can we re-prioritize budget within Q4 to keep SE hires?

[04:55] Oliver: We can shuffle some discretionary spend but I need leadership signoff.

[05:02] Maya: We'll take an offline to decide which hires are non-negotiable.

[05:10] -- People Ops / Compensation --

[05:12] Avery: Compensation calibration — note: we've pushed the schedule because we wanted to centralize the data. We will run a slack forum next Thursday and post the calibration slides. I've heard feedback about timing and transparency. This forum is the place to comment.

[05:30] Employee (anonymous): Any update on parental leave improvements?

[05:33] Avery: Yes, policy is being extended to 18 weeks for primary caregivers, and we expect that to roll out in the next payroll cycle. HR will send details.

[05:44] -- Reliability bounty program proposed --

[05:46] Nora: Quick pitch: small reward pool to encourage post-incident fixes and valuable runbook contributions. Example bounties: 1) fix a flaky metric 2) improve a test harness for KV cache 3) write a clear runbook for fallback routing. Rewards could be $500-$2000 equivalent in points.

[06:05] Liam: I like it. Incentivizes ownership. We'll need a clear governance doc.

[06:14] -- Technical deep dive preview --

[06:16] Priya: Short preview for the post all-hands tech session next week: we'll demo a fallback policy that routes to quantized model variants when the main pool saturates. The aim is to show graceful degradation and cost tradeoffs.

[06:33] Diego: We'll include a simple chart: latency vs cost per 1k tokens for 3variants. Expect to run it in staging with synthetic load.

[06:45] -- Questions on audit logs / compliance --

[06:47] Renee: Sales need an audit logs example for customer decks. Can Security share a redlined doc?

[06:52] Liam: Security is preparing a SOC2 package and a short security FAQ that lists KMS options, log retention windows, SSO integrations and encryption details. We'll share by Friday.

[07:02] Oliver: If Private requires HSM support there will be margin implications; we'll price accordingly.

[07:12] -- Cross-team alignment request --

[07:13] Maya: Action item for all execs: by EOD Monday send two non-negotiable hires, two deferrable hires and top three product risks. We'll consolidate in the leadership worksheet.

[07:28] -- Misc / shoutouts --

[07:30] Maya: Quick shoutout to the SREs and SEs — the Dedicated beta cut customer onboarding time in half. Amazing work.

[07:40] Avery: Also kudos to People for the new parental leave adjustments.

[07:47] -- Closing & recurrence --

[07:48] Avery: We'll run this crew habitat brief monthly for a quarter and then switch to once per-quarter if the cadence sticks. Next one scheduled 10/12.

[07:56] Maya: Final note — keep the lens on customers and don't hesitate to elevate blockers early. Thanks everyone.

[08:02] (informal follow-up chat and partial crosstalk; some speakers unlabeled)

[08:20] End meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (e.g., "kv cache" sometimes appears as "kv cash"), speaker labels may be generic for some interjections.
